title: Read a list-of-strings setting that arrives as Object

blocks.text: The gateway reads its CORS origins with `settings.strings("allowed-origins")`. The setting comes from three places: a YAML file (a `List`), the command line (a `String[]`), or a plugin written against an older API (an `Object[]`). Last week someone wrote a port number into the YAML list. Startup went fine, and the first browser request failed with a `ClassCastException` deep in the CORS filter.

Finish `stringList(Object value)` in `src/main/java/practice/Settings.java`. It returns the strings, in order, from a list or an array whose items are all strings, and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for any other value, so a bad setting stops the gateway at startup and never reaches the filter. About fifteen lines.

cases.says: a list of strings comes back with the same strings in the same order
a value that is neither a list nor an array is refused with IllegalArgumentException
a list holding a number is refused when the setting is read, not when an item is used later
an Object[] whose items are all strings is accepted
an int[] is refused with IllegalArgumentException, not a ClassCastException
a list holding null is refused, since null is not a string

origin.section: Arrays Keep Their Element Type at Run Time; Generic Types Lose Their Type Arguments

concepts: An array's class is fixed when it is created: a String[] is an Object[], an Object[] holding strings is not a String[], and an int[] is not an Object[].

A generic type keeps no type argument at run time, so an unchecked cast to List<String> checks only List and the ClassCastException comes later, where an item is read; each item must be tested instead.
